description:
FILED s510 (s508a agent) from the reviewing session's probe ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s510/review/p8b/kw.pl (rows 15 and 30; answers kw.perl / kw.main / kw.tree).  PRE-EXISTING on main a24b1d65 and on the s508a tree alike; both are LOUD (a die), not silent.

1. A METHOD named like a handle-taking builtin, with two bareword arguments, under no strict subs:
     package C; sub open { shift; join ",", @_ } package main; my $o = bless {}, "C"; print $o->open(zz, yy), "\n";
   perl: zz,yy      PCL: dies "The variable zz is unbound" (the barewords load bare CL symbols).
   `$o->pipe(zz)` and `$o->m(zz)` (one argument) are right since s508a #2664; the two-argument element arm (`_is_sole_call_argument($tok, 1)`) is asked only for a REGISTERED handle name, so an unregistered word in a multi-element method argument list still emits a bare symbol.
2. `require(File::Basename)` WITH parentheses:
     require(File::Basename); print "ok\n";
   perl: loads the module, prints ok.   PCL: dies "Undefined subroutine &File::Basename".  The paren-less `require File::Basename` works.
Fix direction: (1) belongs to the #266/#2664 classifier (a bareword element of a method's argument list with no callable verdict is its text); (2) the require operand parse should treat a parenthesised bareword module name as the module, as the paren-less spelling does.  Guard rows in Pl/t/bareword-call-01.t; re-run kw.pl after.
subject: A method named like a handle builtin with two bareword args ($o->open(zz, yy)) dies 'variable zz is unbound'; require(File::Basename) with parens dies 'Undefined subroutine' -- both pre-existing, loud (kw.pl rows 15, 30)
